title: Compress the String

concept.title: Walking over runs of equal letters
body: A **run** is a block of equal letters. To process the runs, put an index `i` at the start of a run and move a second index `j` forward while the letters stay the same. The run is `s[i:j]`; then continue from `j`.

body.code:
i = 0
while i < len(s):
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    # run of s[i], length j - i
    i = j

body: Each letter is looked at once by `j`, so the whole string costs O(n) although there are two loops.

statement: Compress a word by replacing every run of equal letters by the letter followed by the length of the run. For example `aaabcc` becomes `a3b1c2`. A letter that appears once still gets the count 1.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.

examples.note: a three times, b once, c twice.

hints: Find where a run of equal letters ends.
Use two indexes: `i` at the start of the run and `j` moving to its end.
Write the letter and `j - i`, then continue with `i = j`.

explanation: For each run, write its letter and its length, then jump to the first letter after the run.

code.python:
s = input().strip()

out = []
i = 0
while i < len(s):
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    out.append(s[i] + str(j - i))
    i = j
print("".join(out))
